items.text: $K_\infty=SO(2)=\{r(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&\sin\theta\\-\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}\}$, $A_\infty=\{a_\infty(x)=\mathrm{diag}(e^{x/2},e^{-x/2}): x\ge0\}$ (a subset, not a subgroup, since $x\ge0$), $H_\infty=\{h_\infty(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{pmatrix}: t\in\mathbb{R}\}$, $H_\infty^-=\{h^-_\infty(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\t&1\end{pmatrix}\}$. Basis of $\mathfrak{g}_\infty=\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R})$: $Y=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$, $X_-=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $X_+=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$. For a unitary representation $\pi$ of $G$ and $Z\in\mathfrak{g}_\infty$, $d\pi(Z)f=\lim_{t\to0}(\pi(\exp tZ,1)f-f)/t$. Casimir: $\Omega_\infty=-\frac14(Y^2+2X_+X_-+2X_-X_+)$; $\Delta=-\sum_i X_i^2$ for a fixed basis $\{X_i\}$ of $\mathfrak{g}_\infty$. Burger notation: $a(y)=\mathrm{diag}(y^{1/2},y^{-1/2})=a_\infty(\log y)$ for $y>0$.

$\mathcal{H}=L^2(X)=\int^\oplus_Z\mathcal{H}_{\infty,\xi}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{p,\xi}\,d\mu_Z(\xi)$, $\pi=\int^\oplus_Z\pi_{\infty,\xi}\otimes\pi_{p,\xi}\,d\mu_Z$, each $\pi_{\infty,\xi}$ irreducible unitary of $G_\infty$, with $K_\infty$-eigenbasis $\phi^{(n)}_{\infty,\xi}$, $\pi_{\infty,\xi}(r(\theta))\phi^{(n)}=e^{in\theta}\phi^{(n)}$, $n\in\Sigma(\xi)\subseteq2\mathbb{Z}$ (Bargmann). $\pi_{\infty,\xi}(\Omega_\infty)=\lambda(\xi)\,\mathrm{id}$, $\lambda=s(1-s)$ with $\mathrm{Re}\,s\ge\frac12$, $\mathrm{Im}\,s\ge0$: $s\in\frac12+i\mathbb{R}$ if $\lambda\ge\frac14$, $s\in(\frac12,1]$ if $0\le\lambda<\frac14$, $s\in\mathbb{Z}^+$ if $\lambda<0$. $Z=Z^0\sqcup Z^{rs}\sqcup Z^{ct}$ (cuspidal, residual, continuous spectrum, as in Strömbergsson 2013): $Z^0\cup Z^{rs}$ discrete with counting measure; $Z^{rs}$ finite, containing exactly one $\xi$ with $\pi_{\infty,\xi}$ trivial and $s(\xi)\in(\frac12,1)$ for the others; $s(\xi)\in\frac12+i\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ (principal series) on $Z^{ct}$. $Z^0_+=\{\xi\in Z^0: s(\xi)\in(\frac12,1)\}$, $Z^0_-=Z^0\setminus Z^0_+$. $\mathcal{H}^0_+,\mathcal{H}^0_-,\mathcal{H}^{rs},\mathcal{H}^{ct}$ are the closed subspaces over $Z^0_+,Z^0_-,Z^{rs},Z^{ct}$, $\mathcal{H}^0=\mathcal{H}^0_+\oplus\mathcal{H}^0_-$ (cuspidal functions), $\mathcal{H}_\xi=\mathcal{H}_{\infty,\xi}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{p,\xi}$. $\lambda_1=s_1(1-s_1)$ is the smallest Casimir eigenvalue over the nontrivial $\xi\in Z^0_+\cup Z^{rs}$ (assumed to exist, $s_1\in(\frac12,1)$).

Fix $\mathcal{Y}\ge1$. For $y\ge1$, $F_y,S_y:\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$ are the intertwining operators acting on $\mathcal{H}_\xi$ by the scalars $f_y(\xi)=\frac{sy^{s-1}-(1-s)y^{-s}}{2s-1}$ if $\mathrm{Re}\,s<1,s\ne\frac12$; $\frac{2+\log y}{2\sqrt y}$ if $s=\frac12$; $y^{-s}$ if $s\in\mathbb{Z}^+$; and $s_y(\xi)=\frac{y^{s-1}-y^{-s}}{2s-1}$ if $\mathrm{Re}\,s<1,s\ne\frac12$; $\frac{\log y}{2\sqrt y}$ if $s=\frac12$; $0$ if $s\in\mathbb{Z}^+$ ($s=s(\xi)$). For $y>0$, $T_y$ acts by $t_y(\xi)=s_y(\xi)$ if $\mathrm{Re}\,s<1,y\ge1$; $0$ if $\mathrm{Re}\,s<1,y<1$; $y^{s-1}\frac{\max(1,y)^{1-2s}-\mathcal{Y}^{1-2s}}{1-2s}$ if $s\in\mathbb{Z}^+$.

items.statement: Let $(\pi,\mathcal{H})$ be a unitary representation of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ (no nonzero invariant vectors), $f\in\mathcal{H}^\infty$, $\mathcal{Y}\ge1$, $T>0$, $h(t)=h_\infty(t)$, $a(y)=\mathrm{diag}(y^{1/2},y^{-1/2})$. Then $\frac1T\int_0^T\pi(h(t))f\,dt=\frac1T\int_0^T\pi(h(t)a(\mathcal{Y}))F_{\mathcal{Y}}f\,dt-\frac{1}{2T}\int_0^T\pi(h(t)a(\mathcal{Y}))S_{\mathcal{Y}}\,d\pi(Y)f\,dt+\frac1T\int_0^{\mathcal{Y}}[1-\pi(h(T))]\pi(a(y))T_y\,d\pi(X_-)f\,dy$, the last integral converging in $\mathcal{H}$.

Let $(\pi,\mathcal{H})$ be a unitary representation of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ (no nonzero invariant vectors), $f\in\mathcal{H}^\infty$, $\mathcal{Y}\ge1$, $T>0$, $h(t)=h_\infty(t)$, $a(y)=\mathrm{diag}(y^{1/2},y^{-1/2})$. Up to constants, $\|f\|^2_{W_k}\asymp\int_Z\sum_{n\in\Sigma(\xi)}(1+n^2+|s(\xi)|^2)^k|\langle f_{\xi},\phi^{(n)}_{\infty,\xi}\rangle|^2\,d\mu_Z(\xi)$. items.text: A unitary representation $(\pi,\mathcal{H})$ of a locally compact group $L$ is tempered if there is a dense subspace $\mathcal{V}\subset\mathcal{H}$ such that for all $v\in\mathcal{V}$ and $\epsilon>0$, $g\mapsto\langle\pi(g)v,v\rangle$ lies in $L^{2+\epsilon}(L)$.

For a unitary representation of a group with compact subgroup $K$ and a vector $v$, $d_K(v)=\dim\langle K\cdot v\rangle$, the dimension of the linear span of $\pi(K)v$; $v$ is $K$-finite if $d_K(v)<\infty$.

Harish-Chandra functions. Real: $\Xi_\infty(g)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\|g^{T}(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)^{T}\|^{-1}\,d\theta$ for $g\in G_\infty$ (bi-$K_\infty$-invariant, $\Xi_\infty(1)=1$, $\Xi_\infty(a_\infty(x))\asymp(1+x)e^{-x/2}$). $p$-adic: $\Xi_p$ is the bi-$K_p$-invariant function on $G_p$ given on the Bruhat-Tits tree ($(p+1)$-regular, base vertex $o$ fixed by $K_p$) by $\Xi_p(g)=p^{-m/2}\big(1+m\frac{p-1}{p+1}\big)$, $m=d(o,g o)$; since $d(o,a_n o)=2n$, $\Xi_p(a_n)=\frac{p^{-n}}{p+1}\big((2n+1)(p-1)+2\big)$.

items.text: Let $G_p=SL_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$, $G_\infty=SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ ($\mathbb{R}=\mathbb{Q}_\infty$), $G=G_\infty\times G_p$, and let $\Gamma<G$ be a lattice. $X=\Gamma\backslash G$, on which $G$ acts by right translation: $\Gamma(g^z_\infty,g^z_p)\cdot(g_\infty,g_p)=\Gamma(g^z_\infty g_\infty,g^z_p g_p)$. $\mu_\infty,\mu_p$ are Haar measures on $G_\infty,G_p$, $\mu=\mu_\infty\otimes\mu_p$, and $\bar\mu$ is the $G$-invariant probability measure on $X$ induced by $\mu$. $\mathcal{H}=L^2(X,\bar\mu)$ with the right regular representation $\pi$ of $G$.

items.term: Metrics on G, X and injectivity radius
items.text: Fix a left-invariant Riemannian metric $d_{G_\infty}$ on $G_\infty$ and a left-invariant metric $d_{G_p}$ inducing the topology of $G_p$; $d_G((g_\infty,g_p),(g_\infty^\prime,g_p^\prime))=\max\{d_{G_\infty}(g_\infty,g_\infty^\prime),d_{G_p}(g_p,g_p^\prime)\}$, and $d_X(\Gamma g,\Gamma g^\prime)=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma}d_G(g,\gamma g^\prime)$. $B^G_r=\{g\in G: d_G(g,1)<r\}$, $B^X_r(x)=\{y: d_X(x,y)<r\}$. The injectivity radius at $x\in X$ is $\rho(x)=\sup\{r>0: g\mapsto x g \text{ is injective on } B^G_r\}$; for $r<\rho(x)$ the map $B^G_r\to B^X_r(x)$, $g\mapsto xg$, is an isometry onto its image.

For $x=\Gamma(g_\infty,g_p)\in X$, let $\Gamma_{g_p}=\{\gamma=(\gamma_\infty,\gamma_p)\in\Gamma: \gamma_p g_p\in K_p\}$ and $ht(x)=\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{g_p}}\mathrm{Im}(\gamma_\infty g_\infty\cdot i)$, where $G_\infty$ acts on the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ by Möbius transformations. (Independent of the representative: replacing $(g_\infty,g_p)$ by $\delta(g_\infty,g_p)$, $\delta\in\Gamma$, replaces $\Gamma_{g_p}$ by $\Gamma_{g_p}\delta^{-1}$.) Large height means deep in a cusp.

items.statement: Fix $x_0\in X$. For every $g_p\in G_p$ there is $C=C(\Gamma,x_0,g_p)\ge1$ such that for all $g_\infty\in G_\infty$: $C^{-1}e^{d_X(\Gamma(g_\infty,g_p),x_0)}\le ht(\Gamma(g_\infty,g_p))\le C\,e^{d_X(\Gamma(g_\infty,g_p),x_0)}$.

Let $M$ be the unit tangent bundle of a finite-area hyperbolic surface (a 3-manifold, locally $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$). For $0<\epsilon$ below the injectivity radius at $y\in M$ there is $C(\epsilon)$ with $|u(y)|^2\le C(\epsilon)\int_{B(y,\epsilon)}|u|^2+|du|^2+|\Delta u|^2$ for all $u\in W^{2,2}$; in particular $W^{2,2}$ functions are continuous.

Then for $K_\infty\times K_p$-finite $v,w$, $t\ge0$, $n\ge0$: $|\langle\pi(a_\infty(t),a_n)v,w\rangle|\le\sqrt{d_{K_\infty}(v)d_{K_\infty}(w)d_{K_p}(v)d_{K_p}(w)}\,\|v\|\|w\|\,\Xi_\infty(a_\infty(t))^{\kappa_\infty}\,\Xi_p(a_n)^{\kappa_p}$.
Let $W\le K_p$ be open compact and $F\in\mathcal{H}^0$ (cuspidal) $W$-invariant with $\|F\|_{W_3}<\infty$. Then for every $x\in X$: $|F(x)|\ll_\Gamma\|F\|_{W_3}\,ht(x)^{-1/2}\,\mu_p(W)^{-1/2}$.

Let $W\le K_p$ be open compact, $\xi\in Z^{rs}$, $s=s(\xi)$, and $F\in\mathcal{H}_\xi$ $W$-invariant with $\|F\|_{W_3}<\infty$. Then for every $x\in X$: $|F(x)|\ll_\Gamma\|F\|_{W_3}\,ht(x)^{1-s}\,\mu_p(W)^{-1/2}$.

Let $W\le K_p$ be open compact and $f\in L^2(X)$ smooth, $W$-invariant, with $\int_Xf\,d\bar\mu=0$ and $\|f\|_{W_4}<\infty$. # Reader departures from the draft (library-horo/main.tex)

Line numbers are those of `library-horo/main.tex`.

## Definitions corrected or fixed

1. **Height function (l. 354).** The draft has $ht=\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{g_p}} 1/\mathrm{Im}(\gamma z)$. That supremum is infinite, because $\mathrm{Im}(\gamma z)\to0$ along the orbit. It also contradicts $ht\asymp e^{d_X}$ (l. 359) and the $ht^{1/2}$ Sobolev bound. `height-function` uses $\sup\mathrm{Im}(\gamma_\infty g_\infty i)$, which is large in cusps, as in Strömbergsson's $Y_\Gamma$. I also read $\gamma g_p\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ as $\gamma_p g_p$, and $\gamma z$ as $\gamma_\infty z$.
2. **Injectivity radius (l. 342–349).** The draft's definition defines nothing: it says "there exists $r$ such that the map is an isometry". `injectivity-radius` defines $\rho(x)$ as the sup of $r$ with $g\mapsto xg$ injective on $B^G_r$. The draft never chooses the metrics. I chose left-invariant ones, which $d_X$ needs in order to be well defined. The typo $d_G(g_p,\cdot)$ is read as $d_{G_p}$.
3. **$A_p$ and $A_\infty$ (l. 86, 107)** are called subgroups but are not, because $n\ge0$ and $x\ge0$. The definitions call them subsets.
4. **Group action in the ergodic average (l. 130, 464, 542).** The draft writes $f((h_\infty,h_p)\cdot z)$, but its action is on the right (l. 61). Read as $f(z\cdot(h_\infty,h_p))$. The normalisation $\nu_\infty=dt$, $\nu_p(h_p(\mathbb{Z}_p))=1$ is my choice: the draft says only "fix Haar measures". A periodic $H$-orbit is read as a compact $xH$.
5. **Harish-Chandra function and spherical function (l. 177–182)** are empty in the draft, so I wrote them. $\Xi_\infty$ is the standard $K$-average. $\Xi_p$ is the tree formula. A numerical check (`scratch/reader/xi_check.py`) confirms that the tree Harish-Chandra function at distance $2n$ equals the draft's formula $p^{-n}((2n+1)(p-1)+2)/(p+1)$ for $p=2,3,5,7$. $\varpi_\pi$ is read as $\Xi_p$ for tempered $\pi$, because Thm 2.3 applies it to non-spherical tempered representations, which have no spherical function of their own.
6. **Decay exponent (l. 283–287).** "$s^2$ is the eigenvalue of the Casimir operator" is garbled. I read $\kappa=1-s$ in the parametrisation where $\varpi_{\gamma^s}(a_n)\approx p^{-n(1-s)}$ (from l. 193), and $\lambda=s(1-s)$ on the real side. $\kappa_\infty,\kappa_p$ are taken as essential infima over nontrivial components.
7. **Sobolev norm (l. 313–318).** The draft defines it only on pure tensors. I extended it to all $f$ as $\|(I+\overline{d\pi(\Delta)})^{k/2}f\|$ with $\Delta$ acting through $G_\infty$. The draft calls its spectral formula "equivalent". I recorded it as equivalent up to constants.
8. **Spectral decomposition.** The draft never defines $Z^0$; its list at l. 254–258 names $Z^0,Z^{rs},Z^{ct}$ without definitions. I took them from Strömbergsson's real setting: cuspidal, residual and continuous spectrum. $\lambda_1$/$s_1$ are taken over the nontrivial $\xi\in Z^0_+\cup Z^{rs}$ (l. 282).
9. **$d_W$** is used in the main proof (l. 584 ff.) but never defined. Read as $[K_p:W]$, which bounds $d_{K_p}(f)$ for $W$-invariant $f$ (`smooth-w-invariant`).
10. **Burger's $a(y)$ vs the draft's $a_\infty(x)$.** In Burger's formula, $a_\infty(\mathcal{Y})$ stands for $\mathrm{diag}(\mathcal{Y}^{1/2},\mathcal{Y}^{-1/2})$, which is $a_\infty(\log\mathcal{Y})$ in the draft's own notation (l. 107). I recorded this as $a(y)$ in `subgroups-real`. The draft uses the letter $Y$ for both the Lie element and the parameter $\mathcal{Y}$; I kept them distinct.

## Statements written or changed

11. **Main theorem `main-theorem` (l. 442–444, statement empty).** I wrote the statement from what the proof concludes: the sum of the three case bounds (l. 589, 599, 620), times the factors they share. Choices:
    - $r=T/ht(x\,a(T))$, from the continuous case.
    - $T^{s_1-1}$ for $\nu_\infty(B)^{s_1-1}$.
    - The bound $(1+\log(T(T+1))/\sqrt T)$ at l. 620 does not decay, so I dropped the "1+" and kept $T^{-1/2}\log(T+1)$, as in the $N(v_0)$ bound at l. 614.
    - The p-adic factor $\Xi(a_n)^{-s_1}$ / $\Xi(a_n)^{1-s_1}$ became $\Xi_p(a_n)^{\kappa_p}$, the exponent of the matrix-coefficient bound the proof invokes.
    - The factor $\mu_p(W)^{-1/2}$ comes from the Sobolev lemmas; I made it explicit.
    - $\int f=0$ added: the trivial component would otherwise contribute $\int f$.
    - Irreducibility of $\Gamma$ added. If $\Gamma=\Gamma_\infty\times\Gamma_p$, a $W$-invariant $f$ depending only on the real coordinate is not equidistributed by $p$-adic averaging, so no factor decaying in $n$ can hold.
    - $B_\infty(T)$ is symmetric, while Burger's formula is one-sided on $[0,T]$; the symmetric average follows by splitting.
    - The alternative reading: drop the $p$-adic gain and state only the real rate times $d_W\mu_p(W)^{-1/2}$. That reading is safe but ignores the draft's p-adic factors. See fog-1.
12. **`hilbert-space-decomposition` (Lemma 1, l. 326).** The draft's "lemma" is notation only. I stated what the proof uses it for: an orthogonal $G$-invariant decomposition, finiteness of $Z^0_+$ and $Z^{rs}$, and the splitting of the $W_k$ norm (l. 330–334).
13. **`height-vs-distance` (l. 357).** "Depending on ... the $g_p$" is read as one constant for each fixed $g_p$, uniform in $g_\infty$. The other reading, a constant uniform in $g_p$, is stronger and the draft does not suggest it.
14. **`sobolev-embedding-general` (l. 365).** The draft states $F\in W^2(H)$ and bounds by $\|F\|_{W^{3,2}}$. I used $W_3$ in both places, consistent with the other two lemmas and with the main proof. The hypothesis "$F$ invariant under an open compact $W\le G_p$" appears only in the proof; I moved it into the statement, with $W\le K_p$.
15. **Cuspidal and residual Sobolev lemmas (l. 416–425).** The draft cites them to Strömbergsson, but they carry the S-adic factor $\mu_p(W)^{-1/2}$, which a real-setting paper cannot contain. So they are lemmas of the draft. Each rests on an imported real version (`sobolev-cuspidal-real`, `sobolev-residual-real`) and on the general embedding, for the $\mu_p(W)$ step. $W$-invariance was added.
16. **`matrix-coefficient-decay-p` (Thm 2.3, l. 197).** The absolute value is missing in the draft; I added it. The stray "such that" is dropped, and $n\ge0$ is stated. The draft gives no citation and no proof, so this is a lemma resting on the classification, CHH and the tree asymptotics.
17. **`matrix-coefficient-decay-product` (Thm 2.4, l. 304).** The draft attributes this to EMMV. EMMV as read (v3, §4.3, (4.1)) is a single-place adelic bound with a uniform $\kappa_2$, so I imported (4.1) as written (`emmv-uniform-decay`) and made the draft's product form a lemma. Corrections:
    - $\pi((a_n,a_t))$ became $\pi(a_\infty(t),a_n)$, and $\Xi_p(g)$ became $\Xi_p(a_n)$.
    - $d_{k_\infty}$ became $d_{K_\infty}$.
    - Added the hypothesis "no nonzero $G_\infty$- or $G_p$-invariant vectors". Without it the bound fails, for instance on the trivial representation.
18. **The S-adic integral formula (l. 540–548)** belongs to the proof of the main theorem. I did not make it a separate node.

## Imported results: what was and was not read

19. Only **EMMV** was read from the work itself (arXiv v3, p. 12, display (4.1)). The draft's product statement differs from it; see item 17.
20. **Strömbergsson 2013**: the author PDF failed certificate verification, and the sandbox denied a direct download. So `spectral-structure-real`, `sobolev-cuspidal-real` and `sobolev-residual-real` are stated as the draft uses them, specialised to the real case. Their locators are unknown.
21. **Burger 1990, Gelfand–Graev–Piatetski-Shapiro, Figà-Talamanca–Nebbia, Cowling–Haagerup–Howe, Flaminio–Forni**: not read. The imported statements follow the draft, and the locators are descriptive.
    - The CHH bound is "Theorem 2" from memory.
    - Burger's integral formula and bounds are attributed to Burger as the draft does. The $F_{\mathcal{Y}},S_{\mathcal{Y}},T_y$ form, with the cusp parameter $\mathcal{Y}$, may instead be Strömbergsson's adaptation of Burger.
    - `local-sobolev-inequality` is a classical fact that the draft cites to Flaminio–Forni. I doubt Flaminio–Forni is its actual source.
    - `burger-integral-formula`: I added "no nonzero invariant vectors". On invariant vectors $s=1$, and the operators are defined only for $\mathrm{Re}\,s<1$ or $s\in\mathbb{Z}^+$.
22. **Bibliography.** `dynamics.bib` is not in the library, so I identified the references from the cite keys and the surrounding text.
    - The assignment of the three Ratner keys and of `Danihorocycle` is my reading.
    - The DOIs of Cowling 1978, Nelson 1959, Ratner 1991 and 1995, and Figà-Talamanca–Nebbia, and the GGPS ISBN, are from memory and not verified.
    - The Einsiedler–Ward entry has no verified bibliographic data; its year is a placeholder.
    - The commented-out keys `casselman2014bruhat` and `benoist2004five` were not imported.
